passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: Management’s discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations (MD&A) should be read in conjunction with the financial statements and the related notes that appear elsewhere in this document. This section of this Form 10-K generally discusses 2025 and 2024 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2025 and 2024. Discussions of 2023 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2024 and 2023 that are not included in this Form 10-K can be found in "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in Part II, Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 as filed with the SEC on February 20, 2025. Our MD&A is provided in addition to the accompanying consolidated financial statements and notes to assist readers in understanding our results of operations, financial condition and cash flows. MD&A is organized as follows: • Overview - Overall analysis of financial and other highlights to provide context for the MD&A • Results of Operations - An analysis of our financial results • Financial Condition, Liquidity and Capital Resources - An analysis of changes in our balance sheets and cash flows and a discussion of our financial condition and potential sources of liquidity • Critical Accounting Estimates - Accounting estimates that management believes are the most important to understanding the assumptions and judgments incorporated in our financial results and forecasts • Use of Certain Non-GAAP Financial Measures - A discussion of the presentation of non-GAAP financial measures 35 NXP has one reportable segment representing the entity as a whole. Our segment represents groups of similar products that are combined on the basis of similar design and development requirements, product characteristics, manufacturing processes and distribution channels, and how management allocates resources and measures results. See Note 1 to the consolidated financial statements for more information regarding our segment reporting. Overview Year in Focus • Revenue was $12.3 billion, down 2.7% year-on-year; • GAAP gross margin was 54.7%, and GAAP operating margin was 24.8%; • Non-GAAP gross margin was 56.8%, and non-GAAP operating margin was 33.1%; • Cash flow from operations was $2,820 million, with net capital expenditures on property, plant and equipment of $395 million, resulting in non-GAAP free cash flow of $2,425 million; and • During 2025, NXP returned capital to shareholders with the payment of $1,025 million in cash dividends and the repurchase of $899 million of its common shares, for a total capital return of $1,924 million. Kurt Sievers, our former CEO, voluntarily retired as CEO and executive director of the Company, effective October 28, 2025. The Company's Board of Directors unanimously appointed Rafael Sotomayor to succeed Mr. Sievers as President and CEO and temporary executive director of the Company, effective as of October 28, 2025. On June 17, 2025, NXP announced the closing of the acquisition of 100% of TTTech Auto for $766 million in cash ($675 million net of cash acquired). passages.text: . 2025 Financing Activities On January 13, 2025, NXP B.V. entered into a facility agreement with the European Investment Bank (“EIB Facility B”), which provides for a €360 million unsecured senior loan facility. The proceeds from borrowings under the EIB Facility B are expected to be used to fund the research, development and innovation of semiconductor devices, technologies and solutions in five European countries. On May 1, 2025, we repaid the $500 million aggregate principal amount of outstanding 2.7% senior unsecured notes due 2025 at maturity using available cash. On August 19, 2025, NXP B.V., together with NXP Funding LLC and NXP USA, Inc., issued $500 million of 4.3% senior unsecured notes due August 19, 2028, $300 million of 4.85% senior unsecured notes due August 19, 2032, and $700 million of 5.25% senior unsecured notes due August 19, 2035. 2024 Financing activities On November 21, 2024, NXP B.V., NXP Funding LLC and NXP USA Inc. entered into definitive documentation to establish an unsecured Commercial Paper Program under which, on a joint and several basis, short-term, unsecured commercial paper notes may be issued. Amounts available under the Commercial Paper Program may be borrowed, repaid, and re-borrowed from time to time, with the aggregate principal amount of commercial paper notes outstanding under the Commercial Paper Program at any time not to exceed $2,000 million. The net proceeds of issuances of the commercial paper notes are expected to be used for general corporate purposes. On November 22, 2024, NXP B.V. entered into a facility agreement with the European Investment Bank, (“EIB Facility A”), which provides for a €640 million unsecured senior loan facility. The proceeds from borrowings under the EIB Facility A are expected to be used to fund the research, development and innovation of semiconductor devices, technologies and solutions in five European countries. credit_strengths.text: NXPI's operating margin remains well above the semiconductor sector median, reflecting pricing power and a high-value mixed-signal portfolio. Operating income covers interest expense multiple times, and the current ratio comfortably exceeds the sector median, indicating solid near-term liquidity. These metrics support the intermediate financial risk profile despite revenue declining over the past three years.

Free cash flow generation is substantial, with cash flow from operations less capex covering a meaningful portion of debt. The company returned significant capital to shareholders via dividends and buybacks while also funding acquisitions. This demonstrates the business's ability to generate cash even as revenue softens, supporting debt servicing capacity.

key_risks.text: Revenue has declined for three consecutive years, and operating income has fallen in tandem, pressuring cash flow. The company's leverage sits above the sector median, and net leverage is materially higher than the sector median. A further EBITDA decline or debt increase could push leverage toward the next threshold, potentially weakening the credit profile.

The debt maturity profile includes a substantial current portion due within twelve months, alongside additional maturities in subsequent years. While the company has a commercial paper program and revolving credit facility available, refinancing risk is present if market conditions tighten. The recent issuance of new notes extends the average tenor but increases interest burden.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is solid but below the sector median, indicating less cushion relative to peers. Operating cash flow covers debt at a moderate level, and free cash flow to debt is positive but modest. The company's ability to service debt depends on maintaining operating income and cash generation, which have been trending downward.

Cash on hand provides a buffer, but net debt remains significant. The company has no commercial paper outstanding and an undrawn revolving credit facility, offering liquidity flexibility. However, shareholder distributions and acquisitions absorb most free cash flow, limiting debt reduction. Refinancing upcoming maturities will require continued access to capital markets.

overall_credit_view.text: NXPI's credit profile is intermediate, supported by strong operating margins and substantial cash flow, but constrained by above-sector leverage and declining revenue. The company's strategic investments and shareholder returns consume free cash flow, leaving limited deleveraging capacity. The indicative financial risk profile is not a rating, but suggests moderate credit strength.

Forward-looking, the credit view hinges on revenue stabilization and EBITDA recovery. If end-market demand remains weak, leverage could drift higher, testing threshold headroom. Conversely, successful product ramps and cost control could restore cash flow and support deleveraging. We monitor the maturity profile and refinancing plans, as well as the impact of acquisitions on the balance sheet.

credit_strengths.text: NXPI的營業利潤率仍遠高於半導體行業中位數，反映其定價能力及高價值的混合信號產品組合。營業利潤足以多次覆蓋利息支出，而流動比率亦穩健地高於行業中位數，顯示短期流動性穩固。儘管過去三年收入下跌，這些指標仍支持其中等的財務風險狀況。
自由現金流產生可觀，營運現金流減去資本開支後覆蓋了相當部分的債務。公司在為收購提供資金的同時，亦透過股息及回購向股東返還大量資本。這顯示即使收入放緩，業務仍能產生現金，支持其償債能力。

key_risks.text: 收入已連續三年下跌，營業利潤亦同步下降，對現金流構成壓力。公司的槓桿高於行業中位數，而淨槓桿亦顯著高於行業中位數。若EBITDA進一步下跌或債務增加，可能將槓桿推向下一門檻，或會削弱其信用狀況。
債務到期結構包括一筆於十二個月內到期的重大流動部分，以及隨後數年的其他到期債務。雖然公司擁有商業票據計劃及循環信貸融資可用，但若市場環境收緊，再融資風險仍然存在。近期發行新票據延長了平均期限，但增加了利息負擔。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋穩健，但低於行業中位數，顯示相對於同業的緩衝較少。營運現金流以中等水平覆蓋債務，而自由現金流對債務比率為正但適度。公司償還債務的能力取決於維持營業利潤及現金產生，而兩者均呈下降趨勢。
手頭現金提供緩衝，但淨債務仍然顯著。公司並無未償還的商業票據，並擁有未提取的循環信貸融資，提供流動性靈活性。然而，股東分派及收購吸收了大部分自由現金流，限制了債務削減。為即將到期的債務再融資將需要持續進入資本市場。

overall_credit_view.text: NXPI的信用狀況為中等，受到強勁營業利潤率及可觀現金流的支持，但受高於行業的槓桿及收入下跌所限制。公司的策略投資及股東回報消耗自由現金流，令去槓桿能力有限。指示性財務風險狀況並非評級，但暗示中等信用實力。
前瞻而言，信用觀點取決於收入穩定及EBITDA復甦。若終端市場需求持續疲弱，槓桿可能向上漂移，測試門檻空間。相反，成功的產品放量及成本控制可恢復現金流並支持去槓桿。我們監察到期結構及再融資計劃，以及收購對資產負債表的影響。
